findings: Mahiṣāsura's humanlike torso emerges from the buffalo's back/flank rather than half-emerging from its mouth.
Devī does not visibly pin the buffalo's neck or execute the sourced great-sword beheading; the sword is only part of the background armory.
The defining half-emergence-from-the-buffalo-mouth iconography is replaced by an ambiguous man/buffalo composite, and the unrequested lion adds a competing mount figure to the decisive confrontation.

Mahiṣāsura does not read as the locked partial-emergence manifestation, and Devī's lion plus foreground asura troops are extra characters beyond the proof's exact Devī/Mahiṣāsura pair; only the rejoicing gods in the high distance are supported by the locked page.
Mahiṣāsura's oversized foreground hand reads with an extra digit and the human lower-body attachment to the buffalo is limb-anatomically ambiguous.

The locked decisive action requires trident contact followed by great-sword beheading, but the sword is not used in the action while numerous other weapons dominate the upper silhouette; the lion is also not part of the locked page-29 character set.
The foreground hand's digit/knuckle structure is malformed, and the man-to-buffalo body join is not anatomically legible as a half-emergence through the mouth.
Devī is dominant, but the required confrontation mechanism is not unambiguous: the buffalo mouth is separate from the emerging torso and the decisive sword stroke is missing.
Foreground asura bodies, shields and weapons are heavily cut by the lower and side borders, creating incomplete figures around the focal action.
The art does not depict page 29's exact pin-trident-sword sequence or the specified half-emergence mechanism, so it cannot carry the locked narration as-is.
The required top safe rectangle is filled by Devī's many arms and weapons, the trident, background gods and storm detail.

findings.message: Depict the Asura specifically half-emerged from the buffalo's mouth, not joined to or riding from its back.
Show Devī pinning the buffalo neck, making trident contact and using the great sword for the non-graphic beheading.
Remove the lion and foreground asura troops; retain only the locked focal pair and the page-authorized rejoicing gods high in the distance.
Correct Mahiṣāsura's foreground hand to an unambiguous five-digit structure.
Clear the full normalized top safe rectangle (x 0.08-0.92, y 0.06-0.24).
